status: Window output projection, row filtering and output directories now use allocation admission; complete window retained-state ownership remains open
contract: appendProjectedOutput is shared by ordinary, ordered and window output paths. Each window projection uses a row scratch scope and hands surviving allocations to its output batch. Advancing or closing the stream releases batch storage.
Post-window QUALIFY uses scoped matches, with predicate scratch released per row. Both ordinary and resumable row-window collection also pass allocation scopes to WHERE evaluation.

Post-window execution accepts an iterable. Unchanged row sequences require no copied reference directory; run output is traversed without runs.flat(). QUALIFY/order cases admit a single selected-reference directory, and sorting admits temporary workspace before sort.
QUALIFY, ordering, projection, DISTINCT, offset and limit retain their existing sequence. Output directory and slot admission is separate from serialized operator limits.

cases: Window projection and QUALIFY expansion tested with and without final ordering. Oversized replace expressions reject under 64 KiB; successful output is checked exactly; failure cleanup preserves a sibling reservation.
Batch size one keeps stable live projection reservations across advance and releases on early return for ordered and unordered window output.

Real Brotli Parquet fixtures include window projection/filter execution over HTTP 206 and ignored-Range 200; Worker R2 coverage uses the same route with 64/128 MiB shared pools and 2 MiB query limits.

Existing window state/resume/spill tests continue to verify output and run partitioning. The 170-byte serialized-state test now explicitly supplies a separate 64 KiB allocation cap, preserving its serialized and row-budget assertions.

limits: Window matched input, backend result ownership, resumable-state serialization and accumulated returned rows are not fully owned yet. A batch-scope guarantee does not establish a whole-window cap.
Source adapter backing, hive augmentation, borrowed references, remaining scalar internals and VM/GC memory remain separate open requirements.
The eliminated reference copies are structural allocation reductions; no CPU throughput speedup or total Worker heap bound is claimed.
Full final release gates and the complete audit acceptance matrix remain open.
